sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: GraphQL in Ruby uses the graphql-ruby gem, and the interview questions centre on three areas: the schema definition (object types, query type, mutation type, custom scalars, connections), the N+1 problem that every GraphQL implementation faces (and the graphql-batch or built-in dataloader solution that batches resolver calls), and subscriptions over ActionCable. The N+1 question is the depth marker — a naive resolver that loads associated records inside a list field fires one query per parent record. DataLoader solves this by collecting all the association IDs, firing a single batched query, then distributing results. This page covers the full graphql-ruby stack plus the comparison interviewers always ask: when to prefer GraphQL over REST for a Rails API.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: types-and-resolvers, mutations, n-plus-one-dataloader, subscriptions. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
